text: Refactoring is the process of improving the internal structure of your code without changing what it does. The main goal is not to add new features, but to make the code cleaner and easier to understand. By removing duplication, simplifying complex logic, and breaking large functions into smaller ones, you enhance readability for yourself and your team. This practice directly reduces technical debt, which is the cost of dealing with messy, rushed code later. Regular refactoring can be compared to cleaning your workspace: it takes a little time, but it saves effort in the long run, making future changes safer and more efficient.
